hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5 million budget cut, 116 layoffs under proposed homestead exemption
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $9.5 million in the first year and $16.5 million annually by the second year if Florida voters approve a proposed expansion of the homestead exemption in November. Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli told Martin County commissioners Tuesday that the revenue reduction would equal a 22% cut to the department's current budget and could force the layoff of 116 firefighters by the second year, equivalent to one of the department's three shifts.

The department outlined potential closures of Station 18 on Britt Road, Station 33 in Hobe Sound, and Station 23 on Kanner Highway. Cianciulli warned that Martin County could also be forced to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations. The department would then have to request assistance from neighboring agencies in Palm Beach or St. Lucie counties, potentially increasing response times. Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas, where outside assets took 14 hours to arrive, as an example of delays that can occur when communities must rely on outside resources.

During public comment, one resident and a commissioner questioned whether reducing employee salaries could help address the shortfall. Cianciulli responded that Martin County already has difficulty recruiting trained firefighter-paramedics because departments farther south offer better compensation. He said when the department held its last training class with 22 open positions, only about three paramedics graduated while the rest were firefighter EMTs, because the compensation package for trained firefighter-medics is much higher down south.

Cianciulli advised residents to learn as much as possible about the proposal and its potential effects before casting their ballots in November. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would need to do belt tightening and slash budgets elsewhere, while Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around. No decisions were made Tuesday. Voters will decide on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Chief warns tax amendment could force 116 firefighter cuts, station closures
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli told commissioners Tuesday that a proposed property tax reform amendment on the November ballot could force the county to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years and close multiple fire stations. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing major reductions in service.

Cianciulli outlined potential cuts that include closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could also be forced to stop backfilling stations with personnel, which would result in randomized brownouts of stations. About 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel, leaving few options to absorb the projected revenue loss.

Residents who attended the commission meeting expressed mixed reactions. One resident called fire service valuable, while another questioned why cutting personnel pay was not part of the options. Commissioners also disagreed on how to respond if the reform passes. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would need to do belt tightening and slashing of budgets elsewhere, while Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county should tighten up because it only has so many dollars to go around.

No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan accordingly ahead of the November vote. Officials warned the proposed cuts could lead to longer emergency response times and affect specialized emergency services provided throughout Martin County. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Indian River County firefighter and paramedic died by suicide in Sebastian home
cards.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue firefighter and paramedic Geoffrey S. Lang, 35, died by suicide at his Sebastian home on Saturday, July 25, according to a Sebastian Police Department report. Sebastian police 911 dispatch received a call from Lang's wife at 4:18 p.m. stating that her husband shot himself in front of her.

Sebastian police officers responded to the residence and entered the property with a K-9 dog to inspect the home. Officers discovered Lang's body in a bedroom with an apparent gunshot wound to the head. A neighbor told police they heard a woman yelling and screaming between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m., followed by a gunshot. The neighbor initially thought it was fireworks but recognized the distinctive sound of a single gunshot.

An individual with Indian River County Fire Rescue pronounced Lang dead at the scene. His body was taken to the medical examiner's office by Lowther Funeral Home. When Sebastian police officers arrived, one of the neighbors said they spoke to a female neighbor who appeared hostile.

A funeral service for Lang will be held on Tuesday, August 3 at Community Church located at 1901 23rd Street, according to an obituary by Thomas S. Lowther Funeral Home Crematory in Vero Beach. The Suicide Crisis Lifeline is available by calling or texting 988, or through online chat. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or texting a ZIP code to 898211.

cards.headline: Fishback stays on Florida primary ballot after judge rejects Collins residency challenge
cards.teaser: A circuit judge ruled that Lt. Gov. Jay Collins failed to present enough evidence to remove Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback from the Aug. 18 primary ballot over residency questions.
cards.body:
Circuit Judge David Frank ruled Monday that Collins failed to present enough evidence to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and access to the ballot. Collins had argued that Fishback failed to satisfy the Florida Constitution's requirement that a governor reside in the state for the seven years preceding the general election. Collins attorneys pointed to records showing Fishback voted in Washington during the 2020 presidential election, filed D.C. resident income-tax returns and signed mortgage documents identifying a condominium there as his principal residence.

Fishback testified that he never intended to abandon Florida as his permanent home. He described the Washington property as a second residence or investment and said he signed the mortgage documents without closely reviewing them. Frank cited Fishback's Florida upbringing, family connections, drivers license, vehicle registration, voting history and business ties to the state. The judge wrote that Collins had not brought forth enough substantial and competent evidence to rebut these important presumptions.

Fishback turned his courtroom victory into a campaign counterattack Tuesday, demanding that Collins resign and accusing the lieutenant governor of abusing his office and the public trust by pursuing the residency challenge. Collins rejected the resignation demand and mocked Fishback as a trans-Floridian. Recent polling has consistently shown U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-endorsed Republican frontrunner, leading the field. A Cygnal survey conducted July 12 and 13 placed Donalds at 43%, Fishback at 12%, Collins at 11% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 2%.

cards.headline: Martin County to ban shark fishing during lifeguard hours after complaints about chumming
cards.teaser: Martin County commissioners directed staff to draft a new ordinance prohibiting fishing from public beaches during lifeguard hours after residents complained that shark fishermen are using drones and remote-controlled boats to drop chum offshore.
cards.body:
Martin County commissioners voted Tuesday to rewrite rules on fishing from public beaches after complaints that shark fishermen are using drones and remote-controlled boats to drop chum offshore and lure sharks closer to swimming areas. County attorneys told commissioners that Florida law allows fishing from public beaches and takes precedence over conflicting county ordinances. Commissioners now plan to repeal or rewrite portions of the county's existing law and replace them with restrictions based on public safety.

Under the proposal, fishing could be prohibited from county beaches during lifeguard hours, when swimmers are most likely to be in the water. The revised ordinance would also prohibit fishing from boat docks while boats are being launched or returning to shore. Chumming directly from the beach is already prohibited under Florida law, but residents complained that some fishermen are using drones or remote-controlled boats to carry bait offshore before dropping it into the water.

Commissioners directed county staff to draft the new ordinance and bring it back for a future vote. Some residents argued the proposal does not go far enough, with one speaker saying the county should extend the ban to all Martin County beaches regardless of whether lifeguards are present.

cards.headline: Martin County School District consolidates bus routes to save $255,000
cards.teaser: The Martin County School District approved changes to its bus routes for the upcoming school year, consolidating existing routes while keeping bus stops and buses unchanged.
cards.body:
The Martin County School District has approved changes to its bus routes for the upcoming school year, aiming to improve efficiency and reduce costs. The new routes, which will begin on August 10, will consolidate existing routes while keeping bus stops and buses unchanged from last year. The changes address a decline in ridership and will save the district the cost of operating three bus routes, saving $255,000.

According to Ruth, the district's director of transportation, some routes that previously had two tiers now pick up an extra tier. Drivers on routes that previously had an elementary and a high school run are now picking up a middle school run as well. They will get paid for what they work. The district also cited a shortage of bus drivers as part of the reason for the decision. However, no jobs were lost as a result of the changes.

Parents can track their child's bus route in real time using the MyReaxium app. The route changes also include activity buses for after-school programs.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue projects loss of one-third of workforce under tax amendment
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue projects it could lose 116 firefighters over the next two years if voters approve a constitutional amendment expanding Florida's homestead exemption in November.
cards.body:
Martin County commissioners heard a presentation Tuesday outlining how a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption could affect Martin County Fire Rescue if voters approve the constitutional amendment on the November ballot. According to county documents, Martin County Fire Rescue projects it could lose 116 firefighters over the next two years, about one-third of its workforce, because of reduced property tax revenue tied to the proposed amendment.

Fire Rescue leaders discussed potential operational changes if those revenue reductions occur. Previous county projections have outlined possible station closures, reductions to specialized teams including HAZMAT, Technical Rescue, the dive team and LifeStar, and delays in replacing equipment. County leaders have previously said the department has few options to absorb the projected revenue loss because about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel.

Commissioner James Blake Capps said another serious consequence for Martin County residents would be higher insurance premiums. Residents within five miles of a fire station receive a break on homeowner's insurance, but those farther than five miles away pay higher premiums. If the county shuts down three fire stations, a lot of people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance. No vote on firefighter layoffs or fire station closures is expected during Tuesday's meeting.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie men flee police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Two men led Port St. Lucie police on a high-speed chase before abandoning their car and fleeing on foot Monday, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving on Southwest Becker Road. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

 The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

 The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility with indoor firing range and tactical shoot house
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie officials cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center on July 24, bringing advanced training capabilities in-house after years of sending officers to Fort Pierce for instruction.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie opened a $28.8 million police training center on July 24 on the grounds of City Hall, just northwest of the police department. The 54,283-square-foot, three-story facility includes a 20-lane indoor firearms range with an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms, and a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The center also features a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for decision-making and de-escalation exercises, a multi-purpose training room for classroom instruction, and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division.

 Mayor Shannon Martin said the project ensures officers have the space, training, and resources to continue serving the community at the highest level. Officer Brittany McNally said officers previously traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training. By bringing training in-house, the facility will reduce recurring costs while allowing the department to train more efficiently.

 The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. Port St. Lucie has a population of more than 260,000 and a police department of 455 employees with 360 sworn officers.

hero.headline: 3 arrested in Fort Pierce after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in home with boarded windows, cockroaches
hero.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home in August 2025, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The infant's mother, Nicole Maxwell, 27, her father Robert Maxwell, 61, and his girlfriend Vikki Koon, 38, were arrested last week following an 11-month investigation. Nicole Maxwell was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street SW in Vero Beach and is being held in Indian River County Jail on no bond. Robert Maxwell and Koon are in St. Lucie County Jail each on a $1.5 million bond.

St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Detective Jennifer Diaz said the investigation began when Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the infant to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital already deceased on Aug. 20, 2025. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Diaz, who has 20 years of law enforcement experience, called it one of the worst cases she has ever worked. The mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce had windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring and live and dead cockroaches throughout, according to court documents. The house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and was unsafe for walking, Diaz said.

According to court documents, Koon primarily fed the infant only twice a day and admitted to investigators that when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. She told deputies she believed a newborn should have two ounces per feeding twice a day. Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach while the child lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon. In the days before the death, Koon and Robert Maxwell messaged the child's mother and biological father, who lives in Virginia, stating they needed to come because the baby had marks all over him. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the conditions firsthand and that the home looked unlivable. She said other children in the home would come to her asking for water and appeared thirsty and unwashed, wearing the same clothes every day.

Four other children of Nicole Maxwell who were living in the mobile home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families. The medical examiner ruled the death a homicide. Diaz said the case took nearly a year to prosecute because it was complex and required outside experts to provide examinations, which can take several weeks or months. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said protecting children is a responsibility shared by the entire community and urged anyone who sees signs of child neglect or abuse to report it immediately.

The house was extremely hot, there was a bug infestation in the home, a lack of food in the home, and the home was unsafe for walking, she said. There was not an entry way investigators could safely use to make entry into the mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce.

Diaz said it was one of the worst cases she has ever worked in her 20 years of law enforcement. The investigation began on Aug. 20, 2025, when deputies, detectives, and crime scene investigators went to Lawnwood Regional Medical Center after the 3-month-old child was brought to the emergency room and pronounced dead on arrival. Medical personnel advised responding deputies that the child exhibited injuries and conditions consistent with possible neglect. The ultimate causes of death by the medical examiner's office were malnutrition and dehydration.

When asked why it took nearly a year for charges to be brought against the caregivers, Diaz said it was a very complicated investigation with the death of a child and that investigators had to seek out outside experts, which can take several weeks or even months. In questioning the biological mother, Diaz said she found the woman showed a lack of emotion and lack of empathy to the child. Diaz, the biological mother of two and the foster mother of 11, said the case was very hard and the way the child ended their last days of life was very sad for her.

hero.body:
Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce is converting its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up free books anytime they visit. Owner Scott Van Duzer has operated a free book program inside the restaurant for years, inviting children to take books home at no cost, but the collection has outgrown the available indoor space.

Van Duzer said seeing children discover new books has been one of the most rewarding parts of the program. cards.headline: Martin County fire chief warns property tax reform could force closure of firehouses, 116 firefighter layoffs
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli told commissioners Tuesday that a proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force major cuts to fire and rescue operations including closing firehouses and grounding the department's critical care helicopter.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing major reductions in service.

Potential cuts outlined by the chief include closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could be forced to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years. Cianciulli said losing firefighters would be a detriment to the organization and the community, and could force the department to call outside agencies when incidents exceed their on-scene tools or skill sets.

Residents who attended the commission meeting had mixed reactions. Commissioners also expressed differing views on how to respond if the reform passes. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said he would support belt tightening and slashing of budgets elsewhere, while Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around. No decisions were made Tuesday, and the presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan ahead of the November vote.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on Tradition commercial site after months of resident concerns
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Driv
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The council unanimously approved the restriction on July 13 as part of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, ending nearly three months of debate over the future of land originally planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development.

 Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission in May to convert the parcel from residential to commercial use. While council members supported commercial development, several raised concerns that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use, leading the council to table the request on May 26. Heritage Oaks residents urged the council in June to reject the land-use change, citing traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts.

 The council voted 4-0 on June 22 to approve the commercial designation after the developer agreed to permanently give up the right to build a gas station. The July 13 ordinance codified that restriction into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring the prohibition remains with the property regardless of future ownership. City planner Bridget Kean said service stations remain permitted elsewhere in the Tradition mixed-use area but are now prohibited on Parcel 11A. The updated plan also requires the developer to install a fence along the southern property line before mass grading and to complete an architectural wall and landscape buffering along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued.

 Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and the decision, saying Port St. Lucie has long lacked commercial development, placing a burden on homeowners. Councilman David Pickett said the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing and called the shift to commercial the best outcome for the corner. Councilwoman Stephanie Morgan, who initially questioned whether prohibiting a specific business type amounted to government interference, ultimately voted with the council. Mayor Shannon Martin confirmed the restriction would remain with the property in perpetuity before the final unanimous vote.

 Cianciulli told commissioners the cuts would affect response capabilities. If incidents go beyond the tools or skill sets available on scene, the department would need to call outside agencies. cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe over concerns for St. Lucie County Regional History Museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the area's cultural heritage and the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes.

 This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county.

 In a statement, St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings. This is just a really fantastic place, and our history is capsulized in this museum here, he said. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.body:

cards.headline: Treasure Coast single-family home prices rise after two-year decline
cards.teaser: Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after drops from 2023 to 2025. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000. St.
cards.body:
Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after drops from 2023 to 2025. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000. St. Lucie County is seeing the highest increase in the region, up 2.3% since June 2025 with a median sale price of $399,000. Indian River County has seen an increase of 1.8%, with a median sales price of $400,000.

 Kelley Decowski, an award-winning realtor at REMAX in Stuart, said the increases are being driven by low supply and high demand. Decowski said buyers should start making decisions now because there are no signs that the prices are going to come back down. Inventory is low on the Treasure Coast, though the market is currently balanced for both buyers and sellers.

 Cara Collins, who bought her Martin County home before the COVID-19 pandemic when prices were significantly lower, said she has no plans to sell. Collins said current prices are higher than she would hope for, and that the market has changed what would be possible for her family today. She said she would not be able to be a stay-at-home mom and be able to afford a home for her kids if buying now.

 Condos and townhomes show different trends. Prices have dropped in Martin and St. Lucie counties and only increased by less than a percent in Indian River County. Decowski said buyers need to come in pre-approved before they go looking at homes, and sellers need to price their homes realistically and present a well-maintained product.

hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
cards.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

 Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

 The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

 Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Mets erase 5-0 deficit to beat Mighty Mussels 11-8
cards.teaser: Jeremy Rodriguez went 4-for-4, and Conner Ware struck out a career-high eight as St. Lucie scored eight runs in the second inning.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets erased an early five-run deficit with an eight-run second inning and rallied for an 11-8 win over the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Sunday afternoon at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers won the seven-game series 4-3 and finished the season series with an 8-4 advantage.

 The Mighty Mussels scored three runs in the first inning and two more in the second to build a 5-0 lead. St. Lucie responded with eight runs in the bottom of the second and moved ahead for good.

 Randy Guzman delivered the decisive hit, lining a two-out, two-run single that turned a 5-4 deficit into a 6-5 Mets lead. Julio Zayas followed with a two-run single to extend the advantage to 8-5.

 The Mets added three runs in the third. Elian Peña hit an RBI single, Jacob Reimer drove in a run with a double and Trey Snyder added a sacrifice fly to make it 11-5.

 Conner Ware took over on the mound in the third inning and settled the game down for St. Lucie. Ware pitched four scoreless innings, allowed one hit and one walk, and struck out a career-high eight batters. He struck out the side swinging in the fourth and struck out the side looking in the sixth before earning the win.

 Fort Myers scored three runs in the seventh against Luis Sotillo, who was making his Mets debut. Sotillo recovered by retiring six of the final seven batters he faced and carried the game through the eighth inning.

 Elwis Mijares worked a perfect ninth on six pitches to record his third save.

 Jeremy Rodriguez led the Mets at the plate, going 4-for-4 with a double, an RBI and two runs scored from the No. 9 spot in the order. Zayas and Peña collected two hits apiece.

 Reimer, beginning a minor league rehabilitation assignment for a groin injury, went 1-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs scored. He played all nine innings at third base.

 The Mets improved to 11-18 in the second half and 44-51 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game road series against the Dunedin Blue Jays on Tuesday. First pitch at TD Ballpark is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Fall Short in 15-14 Loss to Fort Myers
cards.teaser: Randy Guzman hit two home runs and drove in six as the St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run deficit in a 15-14 loss to Fort Myers.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run first-inning deficit but fell one run short in a 15-14 loss to the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday night at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers scored eight runs in the opening inning and survived several St. Lucie rallies to earn its third consecutive victory.

 Mets starter Ethan Lanthier was charged with seven runs on five hits and two walks before being removed with two outs in the first inning. Harry Genth delivered a three-run double during the Mussels' early outburst.

 Mets Answer With Five-Run First Inning

 St. Lucie immediately responded with five runs against Fort Myers starter Matt Barr in the bottom of the first. Antonio Jimenez, Branny De Oleo and Simon Juan each recorded RBI hits to cut the deficit to 8-5.

 The Mighty Mussels added three runs against Franyel Diaz in the third inning. Ramiro Dominguez drove in two with a single, and Byron Chourio hit a solo home run to extend the Fort Myers lead to 11-5.

 Trey Snyder helped St. Lucie pull closer in the fourth inning with an unconventional trip around the bases. Snyder's ground-ball single was mishandled by shortstop Quetin Young, who then committed a throwing error that allowed Snyder to score and another run to cross the plate.

 The play cut the Mussels' lead to 11-7.

 Guzman Homers Twice

 Randy Guzman hit a two-run homer against Ramiro Villanueva in the fifth inning to bring the Mets within two runs.

 Villanueva later hit consecutive batters and was ejected. St. Lucie loaded the bases with one out, but reliever Adam Falinski retired Elian Pena on a popout and Snyder on a groundout to preserve the 11-9 Fort Myers advantage.

 Young answered with a three-run home run over the batter's eye in the sixth, pushing the Mussels' lead to 14-9.

 Guzman responded again in the bottom half of the inning, launching a three-run homer to make it 14-12.

 He finished the game 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, six RBIs and two runs scored.

 Ninth-Inning Rally Falls One Run Short

 Ricardo Paez opened the ninth inning with a solo home run that gave Fort Myers a 15-13 lead and provided what proved to be a crucial insurance run.

 Francisco Toledo scored on a wild pitch and throwing error with one out in the bottom of the ninth. Marco Vargas then homered to right field with two outs, pulling St. Lucie within one run at 15-14.

 Brent Francisco struck out Chase Meggers to end the game and record his third save.

 Michael Hilker Jr. earned the win after pitching 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief for Fort Myers. Lanthier took the loss.

 Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two walks and three runs scored. Vargas, De Oleo and Juan added two hits apiece.

 The Mets fell to 10-18 in the second half and 43-51 overall. The Mighty Mussels improved to 14-14 in the second half and 51-42 overall.

 The teams will conclude their series Sunday at Clover Park. First pitch is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Zayas Homers Twice as St. Lucie Mets Cruise Past Mighty Mussels

The

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

hero.headline: Florida executes two inmates in one day for first time in more than 60 years
hero.body:
Florida on Tuesday executed two death row inmates within five hours, carrying out the first same-day executions in more than six decades and including the second-oldest prisoner known to receive a lethal injection in modern U.S. history. Dominick Anthony Occhicone, 80, was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. at Florida State Prison near Starke, nearly five hours after James Aren Duckett, 68, received a lethal dose in the same death chamber. The state became the first to carry out two executions in a single day since Arkansas did so in 2017.

Occhicone was convicted of fatally shooting his ex-girlfriend's parents, Raymond and Martha Artzner, in June 1986. He is the oldest known prisoner executed in Florida since the state began modern record-keeping a century ago. Duckett, a former police officer, was convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee in central Florida in 1987. Both men declined or offered brief final statements before the three-drug injection began. The U.S. Supreme Court denied last appeals from both men Tuesday.

Gov. Ron DeSantis, who has authority under Florida law to set execution dates, scheduled both executions for the same day. Since 2025 began, Florida has carried out nearly half the state executions across the country. The lethal injections became the 11th and 12th executions in Florida this year, bringing the 2026 total to 12 of 19 executions nationwide. DeSantis oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the U.S. reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976.

Florida Department of Corrections records show multiple executions on a single day were more common in the past, the last being in 1964. Another execution in Florida is set for August. DeSantis, who leaves office in January, has rarely commented on the pace of executions, previously noting some on death row had committed crimes as far back as the 1980s. All Florida executions are by injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart, according to the Department of Corrections.

cards.headline: Fishback stays on Florida primary ballot after judge rejects Collins residency challenge
cards.teaser: A circuit judge ruled that Lt. Gov. Jay Collins failed to present enough evidence to remove Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback from the Aug. 18 primary ballot over residency questions.
cards.body:
Circuit Judge David Frank ruled Monday that Collins failed to present enough evidence to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and access to the ballot. Collins had argued that Fishback failed to satisfy the Florida Constitution's requirement that a governor reside in the state for the seven years preceding the general election. Collins attorneys pointed to records showing Fishback voted in Washington during the 2020 presidential election, filed D.C. resident income-tax returns and signed mortgage documents identifying a condominium there as his principal residence.

Fishback testified that he never intended to abandon Florida as his permanent home. He described the Washington property as a second residence or investment and said he signed the mortgage documents without closely reviewing them. Frank cited Fishback's Florida upbringing, family connections, drivers license, vehicle registration, voting history and business ties to the state. The judge wrote that Collins had not brought forth enough substantial and competent evidence to rebut these important presumptions.

Fishback turned his courtroom victory into a campaign counterattack Tuesday, demanding that Collins resign and accusing the lieutenant governor of abusing his office and the public trust by pursuing the residency challenge. Collins rejected the resignation demand and mocked Fishback as a trans-Floridian. Recent polling has consistently shown U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-endorsed Republican frontrunner, leading the field. A Cygnal survey conducted July 12 and 13 placed Donalds at 43%, Fishback at 12%, Collins at 11% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 2%.

cards.headline: Florida ticket wins $800 million Mega Millions jackpot sold at Bradenton Wawa
cards.teaser: A winning Mega Millions ticket matching all six numbers in Tuesday's drawing was sold at a Wawa in Bradenton, ending a streak of 38 drawings without a winner.
cards.body:
A winning Mega Millions ticket was sold in Florida, as it was the only ticket to match all six numbers in Tuesday's drawing. The jackpot is worth $800 million, or an estimated $344 million cash option. The winning numbers were the white balls 34, 48, 49, 59 and 70, plus the gold Mega Ball 12. The ticket was sold at a Wawa located at 14510 State Road 70 East in Bradenton.

Tuesday's drawing ended a streak of 38 drawings without a winner. It is the largest jackpot win of 2026 so far. Tuesday also marked the third jackpot win for Mega Millions in 2026. The last time a winning ticket was sold was March 17 in Ohio. The odds of matching all six numbers are about 1 in 290 million. Mega Millions is played in 45 states, plus the District of Columbia and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

cards.headline: Florida executes former police officer convicted of killing 11-year-old girl in 1987
cards.teaser: James Aren Duckett, 68, was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. Tuesday at Florida State Prison, the first of two executions carried out by the state in a single day.
cards.body:
Duckett was convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee while he was working as a police officer in central Florida in 1987. He declined to make a final statement and showed no response several minutes into the execution when the prison warden shook him and shouted his name. Duckett became the 11th Florida inmate executed this year.

 The girl's relatives spoke of decades of suffering after the execution. Dorthy Tula, the victim's mother, said she waited nearly 40 years to have him dead before breaking down. Tracy Mcfall-Buskirk, the girl's cousin, said the man took advantage of his badge. The execution was part of the first double execution in Florida in more than six decades and the first time any state has carried out two executions in one day since Arkansas in 2017.

 Florida has now conducted 12 executions to date in 2026, more than all other states combined. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the reinstatement of the death penalty in the U.S. in 1976.

cards.headline: Judge keeps Fishback on Florida Republican primary ballot, rejects Collins residency challenge
cards.teaser: Lt. Gov. Jay Collins failed to remove gubernatorial candidate James Fishback from Florida's Republican primary ballot after a judge ruled Collins did not present enough evidence to prove Fishback abandoned his Florida residency.
cards.body:
Circuit Judge David Frank ruled Monday that Collins failed to present enough evidence to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and access to the ballot. Collins argued that Fishback failed to satisfy the Florida Constitution's requirement that a governor reside in the state for the seven years preceding the general election. Collins attorneys pointed to records showing Fishback voted in Washington during the 2020 presidential election, filed D.C. resident income-tax returns and signed mortgage documents identifying a condominium there as his principal residence.

 Fishback testified that he never intended to abandon Florida as his permanent home. He described the Washington property as a second residence or investment and said he signed the mortgage documents without closely reviewing them. Frank acknowledged that Fishback's filings could potentially create legal or regulatory consequences in Washington.

 But he found that they did not establish that Fishback intended to surrender his Florida domicile. The judge also cited Fishback's Florida upbringing, family connections, drivers license, vehicle registration, voting history and business ties to the state.

 The order leaves Fishback on the Aug. 18 Republican primary ballot. Fishback turned his courtroom victory into a campaign counterattack Tuesday, demanding that Collins resign and accusing the lieutenant governor of abusing his office and the public trust by pursuing the residency challenge. Collins rejected the resignation demand and said the ruling would not change his campaign.

 A Cygnal survey conducted July 12 and 13 placed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-endorsed Republican frontrunner, at 43%, Fishback at 12%, Collins at 11% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 2%.

cards.headline: Over 150 assisted living residents remain displaced after Bradenton roof collapse
cards.teaser: More than 150 Florida residents remain scattered across assisted living facilities throughout the Tampa Bay area days after a partial roof collapse forced an emergency evacuation at Aviata at Bradenton Villas early Sunday morning.
cards.body:
Family members and advocates say loved ones have been placed in facilities as far south as Englewood and as far north as New Port Richey, with medical records, wheelchairs and personal belongings still trapped inside the damaged building. George Mendez, who holds power of attorney for 93-year-old Alfred Perani, came to the facility Monday after repeated phone calls to Aviata Health Group went unanswered.

 Perani, who has been a resident at Aviata at Bradenton Villas for three years, was evacuated to a facility in Palm Harbor. Mendez found an available bed at another facility in Bradenton to bring his friend closer to home but says he cannot complete the transfer without Perani's medical records.

 In a joint statement released Monday, the City of Bradenton and Manatee County provided new details about why the Fire Marshal ordered the emergency evacuation. Officials say the partial roof collapse compromised multiple building systems essential to safe operation, including fire protection, electrical and air conditioning systems. Damage to critical support areas necessary for resident care, combined with the inability to safely complete a full structural assessment during the emergency, made it unsafe for residents to remain.

 The emergency response involved the City of Bradenton Fire Department, Manatee County Public Safety and Emergency Medical Services, and multiple regional partners. All 157 residents were evacuated by approximately 4 a.m. Sunday.

 The City of Bradenton is in charge of the building assessment. A city spokesperson confirmed that city officials and the Fire Marshal were on-site at Aviata Monday, along with flooding and restoration specialists. According to the joint statement, the property owner's structural engineer is responsible for evaluating the building, and any determination regarding the cause of the collapse will be based on that evaluation. The Agency for Health Care Administration is conducting site visits at the facilities where residents were relocated as part of its state regulatory oversight.

hero.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5 million budget cut, 116 layoffs under proposed homestead exemption
hero.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $9.5 million in the first year and $16.5 million annually by the second year if Florida voters approve a proposed expansion of the homestead exemption in November. Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli told Martin County commissioners Tuesday that the revenue reduction would equal a 22% cut to the department's current budget and could force the layoff of 116 firefighters by the second year, equivalent to one of the department's three shifts.

The department outlined potential closures of Station 18 on Britt Road, Station 33 in Hobe Sound, and Station 23 on Kanner Highway. Cianciulli warned that Martin County could also be forced to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations. The department would then have to request assistance from neighboring agencies in Palm Beach or St. Lucie counties, potentially increasing response times. Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas, where outside assets took 14 hours to arrive, as an example of delays that can occur when communities must rely on outside resources.

During public comment, one resident and a commissioner questioned whether reducing employee salaries could help address the shortfall. Cianciulli responded that Martin County already has difficulty recruiting trained firefighter-paramedics because departments farther south offer better compensation. He said when the department held its last training class with 22 open positions, only about three paramedics graduated while the rest were firefighter EMTs, because the compensation package for trained firefighter-medics is much higher down south.

Cianciulli advised residents to learn as much as possible about the proposal and its potential effects before casting their ballots in November. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would need to do belt tightening and slash budgets elsewhere, while Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around. No decisions were made Tuesday. Voters will decide on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Martin County to ban shark fishing during lifeguard hours after complaints about chumming
cards.teaser: Martin County commissioners directed staff to draft a new ordinance prohibiting fishing from public beaches during lifeguard hours after residents complained that shark fishermen are using drones and remote-controlled boats to drop chum offshore.
cards.body:
Martin County commissioners voted Tuesday to rewrite rules on fishing from public beaches after complaints that shark fishermen are using drones and remote-controlled boats to drop chum offshore and lure sharks closer to swimming areas. County attorneys told commissioners that Florida law allows fishing from public beaches and takes precedence over conflicting county ordinances. Commissioners now plan to repeal or rewrite portions of the county's existing law and replace them with restrictions based on public safety.

Under the proposal, fishing could be prohibited from county beaches during lifeguard hours, when swimmers are most likely to be in the water. The revised ordinance would also prohibit fishing from boat docks while boats are being launched or returning to shore. Chumming directly from the beach is already prohibited under Florida law, but residents complained that some fishermen are using drones or remote-controlled boats to carry bait offshore before dropping it into the water.

Commissioners directed county staff to draft the new ordinance and bring it back for a future vote. Some residents argued the proposal does not go far enough, with one speaker saying the county should extend the ban to all Martin County beaches regardless of whether lifeguards are present.

cards.headline: Martin County schools consolidate bus routes to save $255,000
cards.teaser: The Martin County School District approved changes to bus routes for the upcoming school year that will consolidate existing routes and save the district the cost of operating three bus routes.
cards.body:
The Martin County School District approved changes to its bus routes for the upcoming school year, aiming to improve efficiency and reduce costs. The new routes, which will begin on August 10, will consolidate existing routes while keeping bus stops and buses unchanged from last year. The district said the changes will save $255,000.

According to the district's director of transportation, Ruth, the changes address a decline in ridership. She said some routes that previously only had two tiers now pick up an extra tier, such as adding a middle school to routes that already serve an elementary and a high school. The district also cited a shortage of bus drivers as part of the reason for the decision. No jobs were lost as a result of the changes.

Parents can track their child's bus route in real time using the MyReaxium app. The route changes also include activity buses for after-school programs.

cards.headline: Big Brothers Big Sisters returns Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser to Stuart
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold the Big Taste of Martin County food and spirits event October 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart to support mentoring programs.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for October 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast. Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights.

 The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big, according to Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties. The nonprofit said community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event promotion, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

 Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth. More information about the event and mentorship opportunities is available through Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties.

The Treasure Coast offers several family events this weekend, including a Christmas in July vendor market in Palm City and the weekly Rockn Riverwalk concert series in Stuart.  The Downtown Business Association of Stuart is hosting Rockn Riverwalk on Sunday at 1 p.m. on St. Lucie Avenue in Stuart. The free open-air concert series takes place every Sunday on the Riverwalk Stage, offering live music on the waterfront.

 Several additional events are scheduled in Palm Beach County this weekend. The Boynton Beach Night Market returns Saturday at 5 p.m. at Centennial Park and Amphitheater. The free event features vendors, food and live music connecting residents to the local business community.

 A back-to-school family festival will take place Sunday from noon to 5 p.m. at 7715 Forest Hill Boulevard in West Palm Beach, featuring games, food, music and a school supply giveaway. cards.headline: Martin County warned of longer emergency response times, higher insurance premiums under tax amendment
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner James Blake Capps said the proposed homestead exemption expansion could lead to serious consequences including station closures and higher homeowner insurance premiums for residents.
cards.body:
Commissioner Capps said Martin County has been used to the very best in fire rescue services and he would hate to see the level of service suffer greatly if the constitutional amendment passes. Previous county projections have outlined possible station closures, reductions to specialized teams including HAZMAT, Technical Rescue, the dive team and LifeStar, and delays in replacing equipment. Officials warned the proposed cuts could lead to longer emergency response times and affect specialized emergency services provided throughout Martin County.

 Capps said another serious consequence for Martin County residents would be higher insurance premiums. Residents within five miles of a fire station receive a break on homeowner's insurance, but those farther than five miles pay higher premiums. If the county shuts down three fire stations, many people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance. Response times for people living near closed stations would increase, which could have very serious consequences for residents.

 Fire Rescue leaders are expected to discuss potential operational changes if revenue reductions occur. County leaders said there would need to be a no-overtime policy for all fire rescue personnel, which would mean no backfilling of stations with personnel and would result in randomized brownouts of stations. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.
