hero.headline: Port St. Lucie men flee police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
hero.teaser: Two men led Port St. Lucie police on a high-speed chase before abandoning their car and fleeing on foot Monday, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
hero.body:
A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving on Southwest Becker Road. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

 The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

 The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on Tradition commercial site after months of resident concerns
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Driv
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The council unanimously approved the restriction on July 13 as part of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, ending nearly three months of debate over the future of land originally planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development.

 Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission in May to convert the parcel from residential to commercial use. While council members supported commercial development, several raised concerns that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use, leading the council to table the request on May 26. Heritage Oaks residents urged the council in June to reject the land-use change, citing traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts.

 The council voted 4-0 on June 22 to approve the commercial designation after the developer agreed to permanently give up the right to build a gas station. The July 13 ordinance codified that restriction into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring the prohibition remains with the property regardless of future ownership. City planner Bridget Kean said service stations remain permitted elsewhere in the Tradition mixed-use area but are now prohibited on Parcel 11A. The updated plan also requires the developer to install a fence along the southern property line before mass grading and to complete an architectural wall and landscape buffering along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued.

 Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and the decision, saying Port St. Lucie has long lacked commercial development, placing a burden on homeowners. Councilman David Pickett said the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing and called the shift to commercial the best outcome for the corner. Councilwoman Stephanie Morgan, who initially questioned whether prohibiting a specific business type amounted to government interference, ultimately voted with the council. Mayor Shannon Martin confirmed the restriction would remain with the property in perpetuity before the final unanimous vote.

cards.headline: 2 men force victim to withdraw cash at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce armed robbery
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are searching for two men in their early 20s who forced a victim to withdraw cash at gunpoint from a Wells Fargo ATM on Sunday night.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce became the victim of an armed robbery on Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. when two men forced him to pull out cash before fleeing on foot. The Fort Pierce Police Department said one of the men displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash. Officers responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects, but the suspects were not located.

 Police described the suspects as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt. The Fort Pierce Police Department is asking anyone with information to contact the department.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility with indoor firing range and tactical shoot house
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie officials cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center on July 24, bringing advanced training capabilities in-house after years of sending officers to Fort Pierce for instruction.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie opened a $28.8 million police training center on July 24 on the grounds of City Hall, just northwest of the police department. The 54,283-square-foot, three-story facility includes a 20-lane indoor firearms range with an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms, and a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The center also features a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for decision-making and de-escalation exercises, a multi-purpose training room for classroom instruction, and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division.

 Mayor Shannon Martin said the project ensures officers have the space, training, and resources to continue serving the community at the highest level. Officer Brittany McNally said officers previously traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training. By bringing training in-house, the facility will reduce recurring costs while allowing the department to train more efficiently.

 The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. Port St. Lucie has a population of more than 260,000 and a police department of 455 employees with 360 sworn officers.

cards.headline: 3 arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce home
cards.teaser: Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile
cards.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home last August. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, on Tuesday. The investigation began on August 20, 2025, when deputies responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the 3-month-old to the emergency room, where the child was pronounced dead.

 The medical examiner determined the infant died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Detective Jennifer Diaz of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said the case is one of the worst she has encountered in 20 years of law enforcement.

 Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and admitted that when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. The child lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at a mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach.

 Investigators described the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. Diaz said the house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and a lack of food. A neighbor named Suzan said she had witnessed the conditions firsthand and described the home as unlivable.

 She said one of the other children in the home would come to her door asking for water. Four other children who were living in the mobile home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families.

 Robert Maxwell and Vikki Koon are in the St. Lucie County Jail, each on a $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell is in the Indian River County Jail on no bond. She was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street Southwest in Vero Beach.

 Diaz said the Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before. Sheriff Richard Del Toro urged the public to report any signs of child abuse or neglect, stating that one phone call can be the difference between a child receiving help and a life being saved.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police seek help identifying suspects in Recreation Center vandalism and vehicle burglaries
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are asking for the public's help identifying people shown in surveillance images connected to two separate investigations involving vandalism at the Fort Pierce Recreation Center and vehicle burglaries in the Lawnwood Circle area.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police are asking for the public's help identifying people shown in surveillance images connected to two separate investigations involving vandalism and vehicle burglaries. Police said the vandalism occurred at about 4 p.m. July 24 at the Fort Pierce Recreation Center, located at 903 S.

 An unidentified woman was captured on camera damaging city property. Police said multiple air-conditioning units, a trailer and a storage shed were damaged.

 The second investigation involves a series of vehicle burglaries reported during the overnight hours of July 27 in the Lawnwood Circle area. Police said the burglaries occurred in the 1300 block of Nebraska Avenue and the 1300 block of Peppertree Trail, primarily between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. Investigators said several vehicles were burglarized.

 Some had been left unlocked, while others had windows smashed to gain entry. Surveillance footage showed several people in the area wearing hoodies, shorts and backpacks.

 The department stressed that the vandalism and vehicle burglary cases are separate investigations. Anyone who recognizes the people pictured or has information about either case is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-467-6800 or 772-462-6800. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at tcwatch.org. Police also reminded residents to lock their vehicles, remove valuables from plain view and report suspicious activity immediately.

cards.headline: St. Lucie detective calls Fort Pierce baby death case one of worst in 20-year career
cards.teaser: Detective Jennifer Diaz described the Fort Pierce mobile home where a 3-month-old infant died as extremely hot with a bug infestation and unsafe for walking.
cards.body:
Detective Jennifer Diaz of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office called the death of a 3-month-old infant in Fort Pierce one of the worst cases she has worked in her 20-year law enforcement career. The mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle was in pretty bad condition, extremely hot, with a bug infestation and a lack of food, Diaz said during a press briefing on July 27. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach.

 The investigation began on August 20, 2025, when deputies went to Lawnwood Regional Medical Center after the 3-month-old child was brought to the emergency room and pronounced dead on arrival. The ultimate causes of death determined by the medical examiner were malnutrition and dehydration. Diaz said the investigation took nearly a year because it was very complicated and required seeking outside experts. The child's mother, Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's grandfather, Robert Maxwell, 61, and his girlfriend, Vikki Koon, 38, were arrested and charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse.

hero.headline: Indian River County firefighter and paramedic died by suicide in Sebastian home
hero.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue firefighter and paramedic Geoffrey S. Lang, 35, died by suicide at his Sebastian home on Saturday, July 25, according to a Sebastian Police Department report. Sebastian police 911 dispatch received a call from Lang's wife at 4:18 p.m. stating that her husband shot himself in front of her.

Sebastian police officers responded to the residence and entered the property with a K-9 dog to inspect the home. Officers discovered Lang's body in a bedroom with an apparent gunshot wound to the head. A neighbor told police they heard a woman yelling and screaming between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m., followed by a gunshot. The neighbor initially thought it was fireworks but recognized the distinctive sound of a single gunshot.

An individual with Indian River County Fire Rescue pronounced Lang dead at the scene. His body was taken to the medical examiner's office by Lowther Funeral Home. When Sebastian police officers arrived, one of the neighbors said they spoke to a female neighbor who appeared hostile.

A funeral service for Lang will be held on Tuesday, August 3 at Community Church located at 1901 23rd Street, according to an obituary by Thomas S. Lowther Funeral Home Crematory in Vero Beach. The Suicide Crisis Lifeline is available by calling or texting 988, or through online chat. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or texting a ZIP code to 898211.

cards.headline: Indian River County Fire Rescue visits Dodgertown Elementary for career fair
cards.teaser: Firefighters spent time with students at Dodgertown Elementary in Vero Beach, introducing them to careers in the fire service.
cards.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue participated in a career fair at Dodgertown Elementary at 4350 43rd Street in Vero Beach on Tuesday, July 28. Fire Rescue said its firefighters enjoyed spending time with students, sharing what it is like to serve the community while introducing the students to the many rewarding careers in the fire service.

Firefighters answered questions from students and showed off equipment during the event. Indian River County Fire Rescue said in a statement posted on Facebook that it was a fantastic day of learning and inspiration. Fire Rescue added it hopes to inspire the next generation of firefighters, paramedics and public servants.

cards.headline: Recycled fishing line becomes friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art Aug. 8
cards.teaser: Discarded fishing line will be transformed into friendship bracelets when the Vero Beach Museum of Art teams up with Coastal Connections for a free Second Saturday program beginnin
cards.body:
Discarded fishing line will be transformed into friendship bracelets when the Vero Beach Museum of Art teams up with Coastal Connections for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8. Coastal Connections will lead the hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways.

 Participants can also learn about the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

 The event includes docent-led mini-tours, studio art projects and opportunities to learn about protecting local marine life. From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can then participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions.

 Guests can also tour the museum's summer exhibitions throughout the day. James Prosek: At Work is on view in the Holmes Gallery, while Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases is displayed in the Schumann and Titelman galleries. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day.

 Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership is an example of working with the community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment. Additional programs may include performances, lectures, films and other arts and humanities offerings on select Saturdays.

cards.headline: 3 arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce home
cards.teaser: Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile
cards.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home last August. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, on Tuesday. The investigation began on August 20, 2025, when deputies responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the 3-month-old to the emergency room, where the child was pronounced dead.

 The medical examiner determined the infant died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Detective Jennifer Diaz of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said the case is one of the worst she has encountered in 20 years of law enforcement.

 Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and admitted that when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. The child lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at a mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach.

 Investigators described the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. Diaz said the house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and a lack of food. A neighbor named Suzan said she had witnessed the conditions firsthand and described the home as unlivable.

 She said one of the other children in the home would come to her door asking for water. Four other children who were living in the mobile home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families.

 Robert Maxwell and Vikki Koon are in the St. Lucie County Jail, each on a $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell is in the Indian River County Jail on no bond. She was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street Southwest in Vero Beach.

 Diaz said the Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before. Sheriff Richard Del Toro urged the public to report any signs of child abuse or neglect, stating that one phone call can be the difference between a child receiving help and a life being saved.

cards.headline: Cyclist rides through Vero Beach on 2,600-mile journey from Key West to Maine
cards.teaser: A Boston cyclist rode through Vero Beach this week on a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine to honor a friend lost to colorectal cancer.
cards.body:
Jay Weedall traveled to South Florida to begin the journey, with a goal of raising $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center. Weedall began his journey in Key West, pedaling 155 miles to Miami on day one. He set off on his second leg, a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach, after filling his hydration pack with ice to stay cool.

 Weedall is riding roughly 150 miles a day up the coast through nearly every state all the way to the Pan Mass Challenge. He will do the Pan Mass Challenge across Massachusetts on August 2 and continue to the Canadian border in Maine. By avoiding highways, Weedall says the route offers something unexpected, allowing him to experience little coastal towns along the inlets. Fans can follow Weedall's journey on the cycling app Strava.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Police Department honors service of Indian River County firefighter
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands with Indian River County Fire Rescue following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who passed away while off duty. The department said its thoughts are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time and that it honors his service and the impact he made on the community.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue announced Lang's death Saturday night and thanked neighboring agencies that quickly shared messages of support following the announcement. The Sebastian Police Department said it stands alongside its brothers and sisters of Indian River County Fire Rescue as they mourn the heartbreaking loss and that Lang's dedication, courage and commitment to serving others will never be forgotten.

cards.headline: Sebastian Police, Vero Beach Police honor Indian River County firefighter Geoffrey Lang
cards.teaser: Multiple law enforcement agencies across Indian River County expressed condolences following the death of Firefighter/Paramedic Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Sebastian Police Department said it was standing alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning Lang's death. "Your bravery and service will always be remembered," the department wrote. The Vero Beach Police Department also shared its condolences, saying it stands alongside IRCFR during the difficult time.

 "Our thoughts are with his family, loved ones, and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time," the Vero Beach Police Department said. "We honor his service and the impact he made on our community." Indian River County Fire Rescue posted a photo on its Facebook page Saturday night acknowledging the end of watch for Lang.

 The Indian River County Sheriff's Office also expressed condolences. Anna Kirkland, Indian River Mosquito Control District Seat 2, said she was praying for Lang's family, friends, and the entire Indian River County Fire Rescue family. She thanked Lang for his service to the community.
